identity.title: OLCC Recreational Marijuana Producer License (Tier II, Indoor): Bailey Hill premises, 2026–2027 term

scan.summary: This is Evergreen Botanicals' state license from the OLCC to grow recreational marijuana at 2210 Bailey Hill Road (Tier II indoor, up to 10,000 sq ft of mature plant canopy). The current term runs March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it to fix. What matters is renewing on time and being able to show you meet its five conditions: premises only, annual renewal, CTS tracking and worker permits, video surveillance, and reporting changes ahead of time.
scan.freshness_note: This is the current term, issued March 3, 2026 (page 1), so no newer version should exist yet. It expires March 2, 2027, about five months from today. The license says the renewal application and fee must reach the Commission by February 10, 2027, which is 20 days before expiry. Plan to file well before that date.

conditions.title: The license covers only the named premises (2210 Bailey Hill Road) and cannot be transferred to another location or person
conditions.evidence_expected: An OLCC-approved premises diagram that matches how the site is actually laid out, and records showing no licensed activity at any other address

conditions.title: Renew every year. The complete renewal application and fee must reach the OLCC at least 20 days before expiry
conditions.evidence_expected: The submitted renewal application, proof the renewal fee was paid, and the OLCC's receipt or confirmation date, dated on or before February 10, 2027

conditions.title: Track every marijuana item in the Cannabis Tracking System (Metrc)
conditions.evidence_expected: CTS/Metrc records that match physical inventory, plant tags and transfer manifests, and results of your own inventory reconciliations

conditions.title: Every employee who handles marijuana items must hold a current OLCC marijuana worker permit
conditions.evidence_expected: A roster of employees who handle marijuana, with each person's worker permit number and expiration date, plus copies of the permits

conditions.title: Keep video surveillance that meets OAR 845-025-1450 and keep recordings for at least 90 days
conditions.evidence_expected: A camera coverage map, a system maintenance or outage log, and proof the system holds at least 90 days of footage (storage settings or sample retrieval)

conditions.title: Report changes in ownership, premises, or financial-interest holders to the OLCC before they take effect
conditions.evidence_expected: A current ownership and financial-interest record, plus copies of any change requests sent to the OLCC and its approvals, dated before each change

conditions.title: Display the license at the premises where the public can see it
conditions.evidence_expected: A photo of the posted license at the premises

deadlines.source_line: A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date.

scan.confidence_notes: The document is clean, one page, and fully readable. Every identity field, date and condition was read directly from page 1, and the February 10, 2027 renewal date is calculated from the license's own 20-day rule. The signature line is blank. That is probably normal for a printed copy, but if you need to show proof, get the signed copy or a lookup from the OLCC's online system. One thing I am less sure of: the current OLCC renewal rule, OAR 845-025-1190, appears to let a licensee keep operating as long as the complete renewal is filed on or before the expiration date. The OLCC's fee rules appear to add a late fee (about $150) if the application arrives less than 20 days before expiry. I have not confirmed the exact current wording, so treat the license's February 10 date as your deadline. The OLCC amended its renewal rules in 2025, so check the renewal steps and fees on the OLCC website before you file.

OREGON LIQUOR AND CANNABIS COMMISSION
9079 SE McLoughlin Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97222
RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA PRODUCER LICENSE
License number: 020-1004763A8B2
Licensee: Evergreen Botanicals, LLC
Trade name: Evergreen Botanicals
Licensed premises: 2210 Bailey Hill Road, Eugene, Oregon 97405
License type: Producer — Tier II, Indoor
Canopy limit: 10,000 square feet mature plant canopy
Original issue date: March 3, 2022
Current term: March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027
Expiration date: March 2, 2027
This license is issued under ORS 475C and the rules of the Commission in OAR chapter 845, division 25, and
authorizes the licensee to produce marijuana at the licensed premises named above, subject to those rules and to the
conditions below.
Conditions of this license:
1. The license is valid only for the premises named above and is not transferable to any other location or person.
2. The license must be renewed annually. A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the
Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date. A licensee that has submitted a complete renewal
application before that date may continue to operate until the Commission acts on it.
3. All marijuana items at the premises must be tracked in the Cannabis Tracking System, and every employee who
handles marijuana items must hold a current marijuana worker permit issued by the Commission.
4. Video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 must be maintained at the premises and recordings kept for at
least 90 days.
5. Any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the persons with a financial interest in the licensee must be
reported to the Commission before it takes effect.
This license must be displayed at the licensed premises where it can be seen by the public.
Issued by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission
Date of issue for the current term: March 3, 2026
Authorized signature: ____________________ Licensing Director
